documents.title: Example Residential Occupation Act (synthetic)
documents.text:
1. Definitions
In this Act an occupier means a person who lives in a dwelling with the consent of the owner, and a lockout means any act that deprives an occupier of access to the dwelling.
2. Lockouts prohibited
No owner may lock out an occupier, cut off water or electricity, or remove the occupier's belongings, without an order of a competent court.
3. Notice to vacate
An owner who wishes to end a periodic occupation must give the occupier at least one calendar month's written notice.
4. Restoration
A court must order the owner to restore access to an occupier who was locked out in breach of section 2.

documents.title: Example Deposit Act (synthetic)
documents.text:
1. Interest on deposits
An owner must keep a deposit in an interest-bearing account and pay the interest to the occupier at the end of the occupation.
2. Refund
The deposit, less amounts for proven damage, must be refunded within fourteen days after the occupation ends.
